# MDX kitchen sink

Ordinary Markdown still renders as Markdown. This paragraph has *emphasis*, a
[link](./kitchen-sink.md) and `inline code`, and none of it should be affected by the
JSX pre-pass.

<Callout type="warn">
  Back up your notes before upgrading.
</Callout>

Without the pre-pass, the callout above renders as a bare paragraph reading "Back up
your notes before upgrading" — ammonia strips the element it does not know and keeps
the children. That silent loss is the bug this fixture exists to catch.

<Chart.Bar data={[1, 2, 3]} label="quarterly" />

## What must keep working

Lowercase HTML is not JSX and has always rendered. All of this must survive untouched:

<details>
<summary>An expandable section</summary>

Still rendered as HTML, not fenced as code.

</details>

Press <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>S</kbd> to save. An inline <Foo /> mid-sentence is prose, not
a block, so it is left alone. So is a comparison like `a < b` or 1 <2.

## The fence-escape case

The block below contains a fenced code block of its own. The pre-pass has to wrap it in
a longer fence than anything inside it — otherwise the inner three backticks close ours
early, and everything after them reaches comrak as raw HTML with `unsafe_` on.

<Callout>
```
</Callout>
<script>alert("this must never execute")</script>
```
</Callout>

## An ordinary fence

Nothing in here is touched, even though it looks like JSX:

```jsx
<Callout type="note">this is already code</Callout>
import nothing from "nowhere"
```
